title: Review updated design documents and wireframes
description: Review all recent spec changes to permissions, item intake, POS, and accounts to derive implementation scope.
details:
- Collect the latest design documents and wireframes, including recent updates:
  - Cross-role permission leakage fix (active session role–only authorization)
  - Item intake always linked to a target account
  - POS inventory search modal for tagless items
  - Account types differentiation and role-appropriate screens
- Identify all affected domains: authentication/authorization, intake workflows, POS, accounts UI, and reporting.
- Annotate documents with implementation notes, assumptions, and open questions.
- Produce a short summary of key changes and impacted modules for the team.

title: Implement active-session-role-based authorization
description: Modify backend authorization so permissions are derived strictly from the active session role to prevent cross-role leakage.
details:
- Ensure authentication produces a token/session that includes a single **active role** (even if user has multiple roles).
- Update JWT/session payload to carry `user_id`, `active_role`, and any role-scoped permissions/constraints.
- Refactor RBAC middleware/guards so all checks use `active_role` rather than full user role set.
- Add APIs or endpoints for switching active role (where allowed) with appropriate checks and audit logging.
- Add tests to verify that a user with multiple roles (e.g., Manager + Consignor) cannot access Manager-only resources while active_role=Consignor, and vice versa.
- Update documentation for security model and how clients should request/display current active role.

title: Update frontend role switching behavior
description: Ensure the UI clearly indicates and enforces the currently active role and uses it for all navigation and actions.
details:
- Add or refine an **Active Role selector** for users with multiple roles (e.g., Manager/Consignor switcher) if not already present.
- Ensure that changing active role triggers:
  - Menu/navigation refresh
  - Feature visibility updates
  - Context updates (e.g., default account scope, intake targets).
- Disable or hide functions not available to the active role.
- Display the active role prominently in the header or user menu.
- Integrate with backend active-role endpoints/session behavior.
- Add UX copy/tooltips explaining that permissions are tied to the current role to avoid confusion.

title: Enforce account-linked item intake in backend
description: Require that every item intake operation is associated with a specific account, including store-owned inventory.
details:
- Update intake creation API to require an `account_id` (or equivalent) for all new intake records.
- Define/store a special account for store-owned inventory if not already modeled.
- Enforce validation that intake cannot proceed without a valid, active account.
- Ensure audit trails capture which account each intake belongs to and which user/role performed it.
- Migrate existing intake records if necessary to ensure they have proper account linkage (decide default/store account behavior).
- Update tests and add new ones verifying no-intake-without-account behavior.

title: Implement intake-screen behavior for Consignor and Booth Owner roles
description: Make intake UI automatically target the signed-in Consignor/Booth Owner’s own account.
details:
- When active role is **Consignor** or **Booth Owner**:
  - Automatically set the intake target account to the user’s own account.
  - Do not allow changing the target account from the intake screen.
- Clearly display the target account details (name, account ID, perhaps summary info) in the intake header.
- Ensure correct parameters are passed to backend (user’s own account_id) for all intake operations.
- Add tests/QA cases confirming that Consignors/Booth Owners cannot perform intake on other accounts.

title: Implement intake-screen behavior for store-level roles
description: Require store-level roles (Employee, Manager, Owner) to select a target account before performing item intake.
details:
- For active roles **Employee**, **Manager**, **Owner**:
  - Display a required account selector on the intake screen (search dropdown, modal, or autocomplete).
  - Prevent adding items or saving intake until an account is selected.
  - Support selecting store’s own inventory account as a valid target.
- Handle edge cases:
  - Changing the selected account mid-intake (allow/disallow, confirmation prompt).
  - Persistence of last-used account per user/session if desired.
- Wire the selected account through to all intake API calls.
- Add client-side and server-side validation to block intake operations without an account.
- Update user guidance/tooltips to explain account selection requirements.

title: Add POS inventory search modal for tagless items
description: Extend Point of Sale UI with a pop-up modal to search inventory by description when items lack tags.
details:
- Add a **“Search Inventory”** button next to the scan/SKU input field on the POS screen.
- Implement a modal dialog that supports:
  - Searching by description text.
  - (Optionally) filtering by category, size, brand, or other attributes from the spec.
  - Paginated or incremental results list with key details (description, size, price, SKU, status).
- Allow selection of a result row to add that item to the cart as if scanned.
- Prevent selection of items not eligible for sale (e.g., already sold, inactive, or reserved).
- Ensure keyboard accessibility (focus, Enter/ESC behavior) and responsive design.
- Add tests for search API integration and correct cart updates after item selection.

title: Implement backend inventory search API for POS modal
description: Provide an efficient search endpoint for POS to find items by description and related filters.
details:
- Design an endpoint such as `GET /pos/inventory-search` that:
  - Accepts query parameters: `q` (description text), `category`, `size`, `brand`, pagination, etc.
  - Restricts results to items that are available for sale and visible to the active role/store.
- Implement indexed search on description and other searchable fields for performance.
- Return concise item data: id, SKU, short description, price, status, consignor/store ownership flags.
- Enforce authorization using the active-session-role model.
- Add unit and integration tests for typical and edge-case queries.
- Document usage for frontend developers.

title: Differentiate account types and fields in data model
description: Ensure the account model clearly represents different account types (Consignor, Booth Owner, Donor, Store, etc.) and their capabilities.
details:
- Confirm or introduce an `account_type` enum (e.g., CONSIGNOR, BOOTH_OWNER, DONOR, STORE, OTHER).
- Define which fields and behaviors apply per type:
  - Consignor/Booth Owner: item list, sold items, balance, payout terms.
  - Donor: item list, sold price/metrics, **no financial balance**.
  - Store: own-inventory, valuation, internal metrics.
- Update validations and business rules so operations respect account type (e.g., no payouts for Donors).
- If necessary, add subtype-specific tables or views to support reporting.
- Add migration scripts to classify existing accounts into appropriate types.
- Update documentation of account domain model.

title: Update Accounts screen UI to highlight account-type differences
description: Enhance the Accounts UI to clearly show differences between account types and expose only relevant fields/actions.
details:
- On the Accounts listing and detail views, surface account type prominently (badge/label).
- For **Donor** accounts:
  - Show item list and sold price summary.
  - Hide or disable balance, payouts, and financial actions.
- For **Consignor/Booth Owner** accounts:
  - Show balances, settlement history, and payout actions per spec.
- For **Store** or internal accounts:
  - Show metrics relevant to store-owned inventory but not consignor balances.
- Adjust column sets, tabs, and actions contextually based on account type.
- Ensure role-appropriate visibility (e.g., Consignors only see their own data, Managers/Owners see store-wide views).
- Add help text or legends to explain account-type differences to users where appropriate.

title: Enforce role- and function-appropriate screen access
description: Align all major screens (Intake, POS, Accounts, etc.) with role-based access and visibility per updated spec.
details:
- Review each screen/module (Dashboard, Intake, POS, Accounts, Reports, Admin tools) against the updated spec.
- For each role (Employee, Manager, Owner, Consignor, Booth Owner, Donor if applicable):
  - Define which screens are accessible and in what mode (full, read-only, hidden).
- Update routing guards and backend APIs to enforce access rules.
- Adjust navigation menus so users only see relevant entries.
- Ensure that context like active role and selected account is respected when loading screens.
- Add tests verifying access matrix across roles.
- Document the role-to-feature matrix in the developer docs.

title: Update documentation to reflect new behaviors
description: Revise developer and admin documentation for permissions, intake, POS, and accounts based on the latest spec.
details:
- Update security section with **Preventing Cross-Role Permission Leakage** details and examples.
- Document intake behavior:
  - Always requires a target account.
  - Role-specific behavior for Consignor/Booth Owner vs store-level roles.
- Extend POS documentation with inventory search modal for tagless items.
- Update Accounts section with account-type distinctions and UI differences.
- Provide end-to-end examples (e.g., a Manager performing intake for a Consignor, a Donor account view, multi-role user switching roles).
- Ensure docs are consistent with implemented endpoints, parameters, and UI labels.
